title: Unified Inference: Q2 2028 Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Michael Chen
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD and requirements, key design notes, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging decisions, and release notes for Unified Inference (Q2 2028). It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer success stakeholders.

## Product overview

Unified Inference is Redwood's unified runtime for serving text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Q2 2028 focuses on improving tail latency, expanding model-routing policies, and introducing the new cost-tiered pricing model for enterprise reserved capacity.

Goals for Q2 2028:
- Reduce 95th percentile request latency by 20% for common chat workloads.
- Decrease per-token cost by 15% through improved batching and KV caching.
- Launch pricing & packaging that aligns Dedicated reserved tiers with predictable throughput SLAs.
- Deliver a staged rollout of model-routing by cost/latency policy and automated fallback.

Success metrics:
- 95th percentile latency for chat (1k token windows) <= 280ms for hosted small models; <= 480ms for hosted large models.
- Cost per 1k tokens (production mix) reduced by 15% vs. baseline (2028-01).
- Enterprise Dedicated customer NPS for provisioning experience >= 8.0 after GA.

## PRD & requirements (summary)

Objective: Provide deterministic, cost-aware inference that developers can configure by policy with clear unit economics and predictable SLAs.

Primary user stories:
1. As an ML engineer, I want to route requests to model variants by latency and cost so that my app remains responsive when capacity is constrained.
2. As a platform engineer, I need predictable reserved throughput (Dedicated) with an easy upgrade path and simple pricing tiers.
3. As a product owner, I want automated quality regression checks (evals) tied to rollouts.

Core functional requirements (MUST):
- Policy-based routing: latency_target, cost_target, region_preference, and tier_preference.
- Automated fallback chain: model_variant -> degraded_model -> cross-region -> soft-failure.
- Dedicated tiers: baseline, burst, and enterprise-reserved with defined throughput and SLA migration steps.
- Telemetry: per-request token-level cost, KV-cache hit rate, and model-variant selection trace.

Non-functional requirements:
- 99.9% availability for hosted API under standard quota.
- Rollout time for model policy changes <= 15 minutes for canary; full rollout <= 4 hours with auto-rollback.
- Data residency controls for Private deployments (EU, US, APAC).

Acceptance criteria (examples):
1. Policy-based routing test harness demonstrates correct selection in 100% of 1k synthetic scenarios.
2. Dedicated tier provisioning automation completes in <= 30 minutes with audit log entry.
3. Evals pipeline flags quality regressions with <= 5% false-positive rate on benchmark prompt set.

## Design & architecture notes

- Serving runtime: continue to use kernel selection heuristics based on model family and sequence length distribution. New: incorporate a fast-path for low-latency chat where KV-cache lookups are prioritized and batching windows are shortened.
- Model routing: centralized policy engine evaluates policies per-request asynchronously; decisions are cached for 60s keyed by route + policy fingerprint.
- Fallbacks: implement ordered fallback chain with timeout thresholds (see rollout plan).
- Security: Ensure model-variant selection does not leak customer-specific topology (use policy-scoped tokens).

Key design trade-offs considered:
- Shorter batching windows reduce latency but increase GPU inefficiency. We will provide per-route config to tune batching vs cost.
- Caching duration: longer KV-cache TTL improves cost but may increase stale state risk for conversational contexts; default TTL remains 60s with route override.

## Roadmap & themes (Q2 2028)

Milestones and target dates:
- 2028-04-15: Internal alpha for policy-based routing + unit tests.
- 2028-05-05: Canary rollout for model-routing to 10% of production traffic.
- 2028-05-20: GA of Dedicated pricing tiers + provisioning API.
- 2028-06-10: GA of routing-based fallbacks and auto-eval gating.
- 2028-06-30: Unified Console updates: per-route cost breakdown and rollout controls.

Themes for the quarter:
- Predictability: pricing and SLAs for Dedicated customers.
- Performance: latency tail reductions via fast-paths and optimized kernels.
- Cost controls: per-route suggestions from Redwood Optimize integrated into Console.

Dependencies and risks:
- Kernel-level optimizer improvements (eng-serving-runtime) need to land by 2028-04-20 to meet latency targets.
- Cloud provider GPU availability could impact Dedicated provisioning timelines.
- Eval coverage gaps may delay safe automatic gating.

## Pricing & packaging notes

New Dedicated pricing model (high level):
- Baseline Reserved: monthly commit for predictable throughput (no burst). Includes 99.9% uptime SLA, basic support.
- Burst Reserved: baseline + configurable burst credits for seasonal spikes. 99.95% uptime SLA, standard support.
- Enterprise Reserved: dedicated hardware pools, priority provisioning, 99.99% uptime SLA, premium support, and private control plane option.

Public Hosted API pricing updates:
- Introduce Cost-Tiered Billing: requests routed to lower-cost model variants when policy allows; customers billed by effective model used (transparent in billing).
- Embeddings: price parity maintained with 2028-01 baseline; volume discounts increased at 1M+ embeddings/month.

Packaging guidance for sales:
1. Start new enterprise conversations with Enterprise Reserved offering when projected monthly token consumption > 200M or when regulatory isolation is required.
2. Recommend Burst Reserved for customers with > 2x peak/median traffic and bursty workloads.
3. For PLG motion, highlight per-route cost controls and easy model pinning in Console.

## Release notes (v1.3 - Q2 2028)

Release tag: unified-inference-v1.3
Date: 2028-06-10 (GA)

Highlights:
- Policy-based model routing (latency_target, cost_target) with canary gating.
- Dedicated provisioning API + baseline/burst/enterprise reserved tiers with SLAs.
- Latency improvements: 15-25% reduction at 95th percentile across common chat workloads in internal benchmarks.
- Console: per-route cost breakdown, rollout controls, and auto-eval results surfaced in the UI.
- Billing: cost-tiered billing introduced for hosted customers; detailed invoice line items for effective model variant usage.

Full changelog:
- Added: routing policy engine and SDK flags for route-level policies.
- Added: Dedicated provisioning API and billing integration.
- Improved: KV-cache fast-path and reduced batching latency for chat workloads.
- Improved: observability events for model selection and token-level cost.
- Fixed: race condition in canary rollout controller causing delayed rollback in some cases.
- Known issues: occasional increased GPU memory usage on specific quantized models - monitoring and mitigation (auto-scale) added.

## Rollout & rollback plan

1. Internal alpha: internal + partner tenants for 2 weeks (2028-04-15 to 2028-04-29).
2. Canary: 10% traffic for 2 weeks; automated evals run daily. Manual hold if eval regression > 3%.
3. Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% (each step 24-48 hours) with continuous telemetry checks.
4. Full GA: enable new Console controls and update billing systems.

Rollback triggers (examples):
- Increase in user-facing error rate (5xx) by > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 10 minutes.
- Latency 95th percentile breaches SLO for 15 minutes post-deployment.
- Auto-eval regression > 3% on canonical prompt set.

## Operational runbook pointers

- Runbook: model-routing-fallbacks-runbook (eng-sre/runbooks) - immediate steps for rollback and tracing.
- Monitoring: dashboards created under eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts -> Unified Inference / Performance & Cost.
- Pager thresholds: P0 if >= 1% of requests are failing across a tenant for 5 minutes.
